main_conjecture.title: P versus NP
main_conjecture.grounding_implication: If NP is not contained in P/poly, then P != NP.
main_conjecture.narrative: The current macro-proof does not try to prove P != NP directly. It organizes the search around a stronger nonuniform separation claim, then grounds the main conjecture by the implication NP not in P/poly implies P != NP.

paper_narrative.introduction: This document should be read as a mathematical programme note. Its purpose is to explain how the current search state grounds the main conjecture in a sharper nonuniform target and to isolate the minimal theorem package still missing.
paper_narrative.reduction_strategy: The reduction strategy is deliberately high-level: prove a hardness-magnification route to `NP not in P/poly`, then close the main conjecture through the already available nonuniform implication. The mathematical substance therefore sits in the magnification bridge, not in the final reduction step.
paper_narrative.leading_route_narrative: The leading route centers on `bridge.001` and treats `MCSP witness family` as the bridge object intended to carry the source lower-bound regime into the target separation regime. The route is therefore being presented as a conditional theorem programme rather than as a proof. A remaining abstraction defect is the mismatch between the witness-family presentation and the Gap-MCSP operationalization.
paper_narrative.frontier_narrative: The current frontier should be interpreted as a small family of theorem-sized obligations, not as an execution backlog. Each queued item isolates one mathematically inspectable route conjecture whose proof or failure would materially change the state of the macro-proof.

grounding_statements.title: Definition of P
grounding_statements.excerpt: P is the class of languages decidable by deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines.

grounding_statements.title: Definition of NP
grounding_statements.excerpt: NP is the class of languages whose yes instances admit polynomial-size certificates verifiable in polynomial time.

grounding_statements.title: Definition of NP-completeness
grounding_statements.excerpt: A language is NP-complete if it lies in NP and every language in NP polynomial-time many-one reduces to it.

grounding_statements.title: Definition of P/poly
grounding_statements.excerpt: P/poly is the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families, equivalently polynomial-time computation with polynomial-length advice.

grounding_statements.title: Nonuniform separation target
grounding_statements.excerpt: If NP is not contained in P/poly, then P != NP.

references.title: Definition of P
references.excerpt: P is the class of languages decidable by deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines.

references.title: Definition of NP
references.excerpt: NP is the class of languages whose yes instances admit polynomial-size certificates verifiable in polynomial time.

references.title: Definition of NP-completeness
references.excerpt: A language is NP-complete if it lies in NP and every language in NP polynomial-time many-one reduces to it.

references.title: Definition of P/poly
references.excerpt: P/poly is the class of languages decided by polynomial-size Boolean circuit families, equivalently polynomial-time computation with polynomial-length advice.

references.title: Nonuniform separation target
references.excerpt: If NP is not contained in P/poly, then P != NP.

references.title: Leading-route source
references.excerpt: A hardness magnification theorem has the form:"A barely-nontrivial lower bound for an explicit problem Q in a weak model implies a major lower bound/separation in a strong model."Typically, Q is a meta-problem (e.g. a Gap-MCSP variant) and"major"means consequences such as NP not in P/poly.

references.title: Leading-route target
references.excerpt: In refined regimes, lower bounds for Gap-MCSP slightly beyond known frontiers (e.g. N^ 1+varepsilon -type circuit lower bounds for suitable promise gaps and input length N=2^n ) imply major consequences such as NP not in P/poly.

references.title: bridge.002
references.excerpt: There exist explicit"meta"problems (including MCSP variants) such that proving certain barely-superlinear lower bounds against restricted models (e.g. formulas) would imply major lower bounds for NP in much stronger models (including superpolynomial formula/circuit lower bounds, and in some parameter regimes consequences as strong as NP not in P/poly ).

references.title: bridge.016
references.excerpt: There exist general-purpose magnification theorems (not problem-specific) showing that certain mild lower bounds for distinguishers/sparse-code objects can be amplified into stronger circuit/formula lower bounds, achieving magnification thresholds below previously known lower bounds in some settings.

status_assessment.assessment: The macro-proof has a coherent leading route and a grounded implication to the main conjecture, but it remains conditional. The unresolved mass sits in the bridge object, the route lemma, and the absence of external evidence or discharged proof obligations.
status_assessment.novelty_argument: The novelty is not a claimed proof of P versus NP. It is a theorem-pair-specific research program: a typed witness object, a preserved invariant, an explicit lemma chain, and a falsification route organized around hardness magnification.
